abstract: On July 24, 2026, FRED announced it had incorporated '137 data series about the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the United States, reported by Alexander Bick, Adam Blandin, and David Deming.' The series come from the Real-Time Population Survey (RPS) GenAI module and now publish as FRED category 8, moving what had been a researcher-hosted quarterly release into official Federal Reserve statistical infrastructure with programmatic API access. The category covers four measurement families: adoption rate (share of adults using GenAI), work hours assisted (share of work hours in which GenAI was used), time savings (GenAI-attributable reduction in work hours), and use frequency (daily use and use-last-week, split by overall, at work, and outside work). Latest readings as of July 2026: GenAI adoption for work reached 43.4% of employed adults in Q1 2026, up from 37.4% in Q3 2025; overall adoption among working-age adults reached 57.9%. GenAI-assisted work hours reached 6.3% in Q2 2026, up from 4.1% in Q4 2024 — the first observation in the series — a 53% increase over six quarters. Reported time savings reached 2.2% of work hours in Q1 2026.
keyFindings: GenAI adoption for work: 43.4% of employed adults in Q1 2026 (RPSGENAIUSAGESHAREWORK), up from 40.7% in Q4 2025 and 37.4% in Q3 2025
Overall adoption among working-age adults: 57.9% in Q1 2026 (RPSGENAIUSAGESHAREALL), up from 54.5% in Q3 2025
GenAI-assisted work hours: 6.3% in Q2 2026 (RPSGENAIASSISTWRKHRSALL), up from 4.1% in Q4 2024 — the intensity measure is rising faster in relative terms than the adoption headline

Reported time savings: 2.2% of work hours in Q1 2026 (RPSGENAITSALL), up from 1.7% in Q3 2025 — time savings remain roughly one third of assisted-hours share, indicating most assisted hours are augmented rather than eliminated
Coverage: 137 series across four families, with 43 industry- and occupation-level breakdowns each for adoption rate, assisted hours, and time savings (NAICS sectors and SOC major groups)
Publication in FRED converts a researcher-hosted quarterly release into official Fed statistical infrastructure with programmatic API access and revision history
methodology: Real-Time Population Survey GenAI module, an online survey of US working-age adults fielded quarterly by Alexander Bick (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis), Adam Blandin (Vanderbilt), and David Deming (Harvard). Adoption-rate series begin 2024-07-01 (Q3 2024); work-hours-assisted and time-savings series begin 2024-10-01 (Q4 2024). All series are quarterly and expressed in percent. Adoption is self-reported use of generative AI; assisted work hours and time savings are self-reported shares of the respondent's own work hours. Breakdowns are published for 20 NAICS industry sectors and 22 SOC occupation major groups, plus an all-employed-adults aggregate. Series values verified directly against the FRED API on 2026-07-27.
qualifiers: Tier 1 — official Federal Reserve publication of a peer-recognized survey series, with the underlying instrument designed and fielded by academic economists. Caveats: the RPS is an online opt-in panel weighted to population benchmarks, not a probability sample like the CPS, so levels may diverge from household-survey estimates of the same construct. All three intensity measures (adoption, assisted hours, time savings) are self-reported and subject to recall and social-desirability bias; respondents may not reliably distinguish GenAI from other software. Time savings in particular asks workers to estimate a counterfactual. Industry and occupation cells have smaller samples than the aggregate and are correspondingly noisier. The quarterly cadence means the series lags fast-moving adoption. FRED reports the series as published by the researchers and does not independently revise them.
